title: Grateful Dead Live at Felt Forum, Madison Square Garden on 1971-12-04
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> Sound Devices 744T -> Samplitude Professional v11.1 -> FLAC
source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Apogee AD500 -> Dat

ai_review.summary: Pristine Charlie Miller soundboard captures a high‑energy ’71 show with smoking Smokestack Lightning and an epic Other One suite.
ai_review.review: The recording is a crystal‑clear soundboard source that lets the band’s 1971 fire shine through – Jerry “killing it” on guitar, Pigpen’s organ and harmonica soaring on Smokestack Lightning, and a tightly woven Me‑and‑My‑Uncle → Other One → Mexicali Blues → Wharf Rat sequence that fans call legendary.  The mix is superb (though Phil’s bass sits a bit low), making this one of the most enjoyable snapshots of that era.

ai_rating.rationale: The vast majority of reviews are 5‑star, praising both performance and soundboard quality; a few outlier negative comments focus only on Pigpen’s vocals and do not detract from the overall high appraisal.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Praised as pristine, crisp and well‑balanced; Charlie Miller’s mastering is highlighted.  Minor note: Phil’s bass is a bit low in the mix, but overall clarity is superb.

standout_songs: Me and My Uncle → The Other One → Mexicali Blues → Wharf Rat
show_quality.setlist_flow: Unusual first set that builds into a second‑set suite of four classics, delivering high verve and tight transitions.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly described as ‘killing it’ with great tone; his solo on The Other One noted as solid but slightly secondary to the ferocious Wharf Rat outro.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass is powerful live (‘Phil kills that tune’) though a bit low in this mix; overall solid foundation.
band_member_comments.Bob: Pigpen’s organ and harmonica receive strong praise (especially on Smokestack Lightning), while a few disparaging comments criticize his vocal tone.
band_member_comments.Keys: Both Pigpen’s organ and Keith Crisp’s piano are highlighted as prominent and jazzy, adding depth to the sound.
